summary: The prepared base reproduced the retained random classification-head bias. At the exact candidate commit, the real Qwen3 load_weights path produced exact bias-free logits when score.bias was absent and retained an explicit nonzero checkpoint bias. Independent GPU cases also passed for float32, float16, and bfloat16.

tests.what_was_measured: The original missing-bias failure reproduced through the actual checkout import and load_weights implementation: all 6 logits differed, with greatest absolute difference 0.29578280448913574. The explicit nonzero-bias subcase passed. Raw output: reports/j-7cc508ea56d3/raw/failing_before.txt
The candidate regression passed exact CPU comparisons for both absent score.bias and explicit nonzero score.bias (2 subtests). Raw output: reports/j-7cc508ea56d3/raw/passing_after.txt

tests.command: /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-7cc508ea56d3/venv/bin/python - [independent inline ROCm numerical test at candidate commit]
tests.what_was_measured: On AMD Instinct MI350X, missing-bias and explicit-bias outputs exactly matched torch.nn.functional.linear references for float32, float16, and bfloat16; the initialized bias contained zero nonzero elements. Raw output: reports/j-7cc508ea56d3/raw/adversarial_gpu.txt

gpu_execution.evidence: One visible AMD Instinct MI350X executed the independent numerical cases using PyTorch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 and HIP 7.2.26015. Exact parity was observed in all tested dtypes.

remaining_limitations: Validation isolates the classification head and its real load_weights path by replacing the unrelated Qwen3 backbone with nn.Identity; it does not run a full model checkpoint or server. The host reports a NUMA-balancing performance warning. No C++/FlyDSL/native source changed and repository-environment.json records native as null, so no native rebuild was applicable. The candidate keeps a zero-valued bias Parameter for bias-free checkpoints rather than removing the Parameter, but the original issue's required head computation and explicit-bias compatibility are both satisfied.
